description: We’re a NASA Space Apps team combining game development, pixel art, and storytelling to build a game about life on a lunar base. If you enjoy making games and want to bring the Moon to life with us, we’d love to hear from you. Skills in programming, game design, art, or sound are welcome.
summary: Mars Watch (Turkish: Mars Nöbeti) is a 2D pixel-art resource management and decision-making game set inside a Martian research habitat during an approaching dust storm. Inspired by real NASA mission findings—including the 2018 global dust storm that dropped the Opportunity rover's usable energy to 21 Wh—the storm blocks sunlight and forces the base onto limited battery reserves. Players inspect telemetry at the central Control Panel and navigate between the greenhouse, water recovery and electrolysis tank, ventilation filter, thermal zones, and radiation shelter to make critical survival trade-offs. Built in Unity with 32 branching decision paths, the simulation dynamically tracks remaining energy, crop yield, CO₂ levels, clean water, oxygen, and crew radiation exposure. Once the storm clears, habitat AI guide Auggie presents the "Path You Took" (İzlediğin Yol) debrief, explaining the real-world spaceflight science behind every choice.
details:
Mars Watch (Mars Nöbeti) is an interactive 2D survival and engineering simulation set on Mars. When a severe dust storm and solar particle alert strike a Martian research station, solar array generation plummets and the habitat switches to battery power. Players monitor system status at the Control Panel and interact (E key) with five core life-support stations:\

  • Greenhouse: Dimming LED grow lights saves electricity but delays crop harvest.\
  • Water Tank (ECLSS): Balancing water recovery and electrolysis affects potable water reserves versus oxygen generation.\
  • Air Filtration: Throttling the ventilation filter conserves power at the cost of rising cabin CO₂ levels.\
  • Zonal Thermal Isolation: Concentrating active heating in occupied zones prevents unnecessary energy drain in empty modules.\
  • Radiation Shelter: Relocating the crew to the shelter protects them from solar storm radiation while automatically engaging the shelter ventilation fan, drawing extra battery power.\

Behind the scenes, a 32-path decision engine calculates cumulative energy consumption, resource balances, and crew health. At the end of the shift, habitat guide Auggie delivers the "Path You Took" (İzlediğin Yol) debrief, connecting each player decision to real aerospace engineering principles.
Intended Impact & Creativity
Instead of presenting planetary physics as passive text, Mars Watch turns real NASA operational trade-offs into playable cause-and-effect dilemmas. Players experience firsthand why off-world habitats cannot maximize power, life support, and radiation shielding simultaneously.
Tools, Languages & Scientific Factors Considered
Developed in Unity (6000.3.16f1) using C# (MarsStormMission, MarsStormStation, StormShift, Interactor, DialogueManager) and Universal Render Pipeline (2D), paired with original team-created 2D pixel-art sprites and animations. Scenario mechanics were grounded in NASA's On Mars, Light Is Energy (Opportunity 2018 dust storm), Growing Plants in Space, Onboard Systems: Thermal Control, Carbon Dioxide (Apollo 13), Environmental Control and Life Support Systems (ECLSS), NASA Watches Mars Light Up During Epic Solar Storm (Curiosity, May 20, 2024), Mars Trek, and NASA DONKI (20260905-AL-011).
